correctness.rationale: For every n>=9, a signed Roman function on K(n,2) labels unordered ground-set pairs in {-1,1,2}, requiring all closed-neighborhood sums >=1 and defending every -1 with a disjoint +2. With weight W and ground-degree sums s_i, T_ij=W-s_i-s_j+2f_ij, sum_(j≠i) T_ij=(n-3)W-(n-4)s_i and sum_i s_i=2W. These exclude W<=2; W=3 forces s_i<=2 and an s_i=2 by a counted positive/zero/negative star-slack contradiction. Saturation at s_i=2 forces all s_j∈{-2,2}, hence odd n and B/A part size difference three. It forces cross -1, B-internal +1, and A-internal incident sum |A|+1; an explicit defender condition for internal -1 is retained. Hamilton cycle upgrade gives odd weight 3, and cycle in A plus three disjoint edges in B gives even weight 4. Verified direct neighborhood sums and Roman defenders for constructors n=9..30 and counted initial odd optima 84,990,15444 by A-internal exhaustive enumeration. Finite checks do not establish the unrestricted lower bound.
residual_risks: Odd classification depends on the internal negative-pair disjoint +2 defender clause; mere incident sums alone cannot replace it. No optimizer count for even n.
